bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: Federal judge slaps 14-day TRO on Paramount–Warner Bros. merger
bullets.body: A federal judge temporarily halted Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, issuing a TRO that functions as a judicial freeze to maintain the status quo pending a preliminary injunction battle. A ruling on the underlying matter is expected around July 22. Paramount faces a legal contradiction between leverage claims made to Wall Street to justify the deal and its denials of that same leverage in court filings.

bullets.title: IREN: +19-20% on $2.8B AI cloud contract haul; ARR target raised to $4B+
bullets.body: IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI cloud services contracts with customers including Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, and Figure, and raised its year-end 2026 guidance. The company is receiving 45% prepayments on new contracts—a bullish datapoint for neocloud sector liquidity. Sentiment on Stocktwits climbed 58% over the past week alongside the stock's ~20% rally, though at least one commentator flagged ongoing management quality concerns.

bullets.title: AMD: OpenAI MI450 ramp begins 2H26; expanded Microsoft Azure partnership announced
bullets.body: AMD flagged 2H26 as its inflection point as OpenAI's first 1GW of MI450 deployments begin. Separately, AMD and Microsoft announced an expanded strategic AI infrastructure partnership: Microsoft will deploy AMD Helios Rackscale solutions—combining MI455X GPUs, EPYC Venice CPUs, Pensando DPUs, and ROCm software—at scale on Azure for frontier model inference.

bullets.title: GOOGL: 'Frozen v2' custom AI chip targets 6-10x token/watt efficiency; deployment by 2028
bullets.body: Google is developing Frozen v2, a custom server chip that embeds Gemini's architecture directly into silicon to reduce data movement and compute overhead. The chip is projected to deliver 6-10x more tokens per unit of power than competitors and is slated for deployment as early as 2028. Google is also separately developing Taalas-like chips that bake model weights directly into silicon.

bullets.title: MU: Back above $1T market cap; bull case rests on memory bottleneck and FCF surge
bullets.body: Micron crossed back above a $1 trillion market cap. Bulls argue MU's single-quarter FCF nearly rivals Tesla's cumulative lifetime total, and the DRAM shortage—which ADATA's chairman warns will persist 10 more years—underpins a multi-year earnings ramp. One commentator projects MU will report over $70B in revenue across the next two quarters. Technically, MU and SNDK are attempting to form lows but confirmation is lacking.

bullets.title: META: Leasing surplus compute to Anthropic; $3.5M+ in unusual OTM call flow detected
bullets.body: Meta is converting excess GPU infrastructure into a cloud revenue stream by leasing compute capacity to Anthropic, diversifying beyond its core ad business. Separately, $3.5M+ in out-of-the-money call options on META were flagged as unusual bullish flow on the options tape.

bullets.title: NVDA: SIGGRAPH2026 product blitz—NemoClaw agents, Synthetic Video Detector, Omniverse MCP
bullets.body: NVIDIA unveiled a series of AI/graphics tools at SIGGRAPH2026: NemoClaw on DGX Station for local desktop AI agents targeting designers and engineers; a Synthetic Video Detector microservice achieving 92% accuracy on 1080p video in 22ms for broadcasters; and expanded Omniverse Agent Toolkit via MCP for simulation-ready world building. Jensen Huang also conducted informal diplomacy with Japan's top 30 semiconductor executives at a Tokyo izakaya.

bullets.title: LITE: Barclays upgrades to Overweight ahead of chip earnings on AI optical demand
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded Lumentum (LITE) to Overweight ahead of semiconductor earnings, citing greater confidence in AI networking component demand and stronger optical interconnect tailwinds.

bullets.title: COHR: Strong next-quarter guidance—$1.98B rev (+29.5% YoY), 40-42% adj. gross margin
bullets.body: Coherent guided next-quarter revenue to ~$1.98B, representing +9.6% QoQ and +29.5% YoY growth, with exit adjusted gross margins of 40.5–42% and adjusted operating margins of 23–25%. The next four quarters imply $8.5–9.0B in revenue at 29–36% growth—one commentator called it one of the best balance sheets in semis.

bullets.title: HOOD: Bernstein raises PT to $160 on $70B+ crypto/prediction market fee opportunity
bullets.body: Bernstein lifted its Robinhood price target from $130 to $160, arguing the next battleground is a $70B+ fee pool spanning prediction markets, perpetual futures, tokenized equities, and onchain markets. Bernstein cites Robinhood's 27M user distribution advantage as a key competitive edge.

bullets.title: TSLA: Underperforms market pre-earnings; credibility concerns mount over target misses
bullets.body: Tesla is trading lower while NASDAQ and S&P 500 edge higher, with traders reducing exposure ahead of earnings amid elevated valuations. Social media commentary highlights persistent target misses, no financial guidance from Elon, declining revenue, and a German Gigafactory ramp as the key near-term positive. One critical commentator argues MU offers superior risk-adjusted returns vs. TSLA.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hits record 11x price-to-sales valuation, highest in company history
bullets.body: Apple is now trading at nearly 11x sales, representing the highest price-to-sales multiple in the company's history, raising valuation concern flags for some market commentators.

bullets.title: INTC: Intel 18A node out-pitched by Chinese Kirin 9030 at 32.5nm metal pitch without EUV
bullets.body: Electron microscope analysis of Huawei's Kirin 9030 reveals a 32.5nm metal pitch—tighter than Intel's 18A leading-edge node—achieved without EUV lithography, raising questions about Intel's node leadership claim. Additionally, Intel Xeon 6 reaches 8000 MT/s memory speed but the higher-performance 8800 MT/s MRDIMM capability has been pushed to 2027.

bullets.title: NBIS: Northland raises PT to $410; 45%+ contract prepayments signal neocloud strength
bullets.body: Northland raised its price target on Nebius to $410. Separately, commentary suggests NBIS is likely receiving prepayment percentages even larger than IREN's 45% on new customer contracts—a bullish read on neocloud sector demand.

bullets.title: Semis sector macro: 14% of market cap vs. 8% at dot-com peak; SOX down 17% MTD
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector now represents 14% of total US market capitalization—nearly double its 8% peak during the dot-com bubble. The SOX index is down 17% month-to-date, with the biggest names trading 10%+ below their 50-day moving averages. $10M+ in SOXX call LEAPS and unusual bullish chip options flow were also detected, suggesting some tactical buying at oversold levels.

bullets.title: Hedge funds exiting tech at record pace; $5.3T hyperscaler AI capex draws scrutiny
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs data shows hedge funds were net sellers of tech for 6 of the past 8 weeks, cutting sector exposure ~10%—the largest sector outflow since data tracking began. Goldman also flagged that $5.3T in combined AI capex from Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet through 2030 could pressure bond markets. Goldman's One-Delta desk suggested market bottom may still be 'a couple of weeks away.'

bullets.title: GOOGL long-dated debt down 7% since February; rising yields pressure tech credit
bullets.body: Alphabet's 100-year Sterling bond has lost more than 7% since its February issuance, hurt by duration, UK political risk, and a glut of Alphabet debt supply. Investment-grade tech debt issued this year has almost universally lost value amid rising longer-term yields.

bullets.title: MDB: MongoDB launches Atlas Revenue Forecast tool to track growth engine in real time
bullets.body: MongoDB introduced an Atlas Revenue Forecast tool designed to provide real-time signals on Atlas—its primary growth driver—ahead of official earnings reports, offering investors an early read on the company's revenue trajectory.

bullets.title: DIS: -11% total return over 11 years vs. SPY +320%—valuation underperformance highlighted
bullets.body: A chart circulating on X shows Disney delivered a -11% total return over the past 11 years versus the S&P 500's +320%, underscoring the stock's persistent long-term underperformance.

bullets.title: ADBE: Launches 'natural look' AI camera app with generative capabilities
bullets.body: Adobe released a new camera application leveraging generative AI, with an emphasis on producing natural-looking imagery. The product expands Adobe's consumer AI footprint though no financial guidance was provided.
